title: Mini-cohort orchestrator with snapshot sanity checks and autorepair for staged rollouts
author: Ava Morgan
release_notes: Introduce a 'mini-cohort orchestrator' to enable tiny, session-consistent canaries with snapshot sanity checks and an autorepair path. Opt-in via rollout spec 'cohort.type: mini'. No default behavior change.
description:
Motivation: We frequently need sub-percent canaries for high-sensitivity features (rerankers, safety filters) where full canaries are too coarse and shadow-only validation produces too much noise. This PR implements a lightweight 'mini-cohort' orchestrator that combines deterministic shadow replay, tiny live traffic cohorts (0.01-0.5%), snapshot-based sanity gates, and an automatic repair flow that attempts a safe retry/rollback sequence when metric drift or stability regressions are detected.

What this PR does: Adds a new orchestrator plugin 'mini-cohort' for staged rollouts that: 1) pins cohorts to session/session-key buckets for consistency across retries; 2) takes a lightweight model + config snapshot at cohort start and computes a fast sanity diff (latency P95, token rejection rate, top-k divergence on sentinel prompts); 3) runs shadow replay for sampled flows to compute deterministic deltas before cutover; 4) continually evaluates telemetry and, on breach of configured safety thresholds, triggers a three-step autorepair: quick-rollback to previous model, localized replay to determine reproducibility, and scaled re-probe with a warmed KV-cache replica. The autorepair flow is conservative: it never increases user-visible cohort % during recovery and requires two independent metric regressions to proceed to rollback automatically.

Config (example): {"rollout":{"type":"mini-cohort","cohort_percent":0.1,"session_affinity":true,"sanity_probes":{"prompts":["__latency_probe__","__safety_sentinel__"],"max_drift":0.15},"autorepair":{"enabled":true,"grace_window_s":"60s","min_sample":"200"}}}

Implementation notes: 
- Runtime: small scheduler extension to allocate micro lanes that respect existing batchers. Micro-lanes share the same worker pools but are tagged to ensure session-affinity routing.
- Snapshotting: serializes model variant id, quantization profile, and a compact runtime KPIs vector to the rollout journal. Snapshots are stored in the rollout-metadata table (TTL 7d).
- Sanity checks: implemented as lightweight sketch-based comparators to avoid full distribution materialization; we reuse streaming-diff utilities from observability-pack.
- Autorepair: orchestrator issues a roll command sequence that is recorded and can be replayed; audit logs include the pre-repair snapshot and the triggers that caused the action.

Testing: 
- Unit tests for scheduler, snapshot serialization, and sanity comparator logic.
- Integration tests: synthetic traffic harness that simulates KV cache warm/unwarm and a seeded non-deterministic failure mode.
- Perf: micro-lane overhead measured ~0.8% CPU and <1ms median latency bump at 0.1% cohort; details in bench logs.

Migration & opt-in: This is opt-in. Existing rollout specs default to current behavior. Admins can enable by setting cohort.type to 'mini-cohort' or using Console -> Rollouts -> Advanced -> Allow mini-cohorts.

Checklist:
- [x] Scheduler micro-lane allocation
- [x] Snapshot serializer + storage schema
- [x] Sanity comparator implementation
- [x] Autorepair control flow and audit logging
- [x] SDK flags and console toggles
- [x] Unit/integration tests
- [x] Docs: rollout guide + troubleshooting

Risks & mitigation: Auto-repair is conservative and gated behind two metric signals to avoid flapping. Snapshots are compact and TTLed to minimize metadata sprawl. We added an emergency 'drain-mini-cohorts' feature flag to quickly evacuate micro-lanes cluster-wide.

Related work: Builds on the shadow-replay and session-affinity primitives created in ENG-887 and integrates telemetry gates from ENG-1022.

Notes for reviewers: Focus review on correctness of snapshot schema (rollout-metadata migration), the safety threshold choices in sanity comparator, and the autorepair state machine transitions.

migration_steps:
1) Run DB migration 20260218_add_mini_cohort_snapshot.sql against rollout-metadata.
2) Toggle infra/feature_flags.allow_mini_cohorts = true in staging.
3) Use Console to enable mini-cohort per-route and start with 0.01% cohort_percent.
4) Monitor telemetry gate dashboards for 24h before increasing cohort size.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps micro-lane scheduling as a non-breaking extension; we may consider a dedicated micro-lane worker pool in a follow-up after load testing at scale.
